summary: An L-4 ground house near Mt. Rainier built in the early 1930s (sources vary 1932-1934), used in WWII aircraft warning, and still volunteer-staffed in summer.

facts.design: L-4 ground house, 14x14 ft, pyramidal roof

access.note: Open to the public in summer; last mile of Forest Road 7315 generally gated unless staffed or work is underway, with a trail from the gate.

visit.trail_note: Drive most of the way on FR 7315, then a short trail/final mile on foot; ramp added for disabled access.

events.note: Wikipedia/NRHP area info gives 1932 or 1933 (NRHP record area says 'Built 1933').
firelookout.com states the present L-4 cab was built in 1934.
Used as a WWII U.S. Army Aircraft Warning System site (precise year approximate, WWII era).
Road to the lookout (Forest Road 7315) completed.
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places, July 14, 1987.
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register, September 15, 1994.
Volunteer staffing suspended 2020-21 due to COVID.
Interior renovated to reflect 1960s fire equipment; trail, deck, and accessibility ramp added.

evidence.supports: Built 1932, location and WWII use, road completed 1956
evidence.quote: Built in 1932, it is one of only two L-4 ground house structures remaining on the old Snoqualmie National Forest. It was used as an Aircraft Warning site in World War II and the road to it was not completed until 1956.

evidence.supports: 15 miles northeast of Mt. Rainier, Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie NF, high alpine meadow, Winthrop Glacier view
evidence.quote: Suntop Lookout is located 15 miles northeast of Mt. Rainier, Washington within the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest. ... Located in a high alpine meadow with excellent view of Winthrop Glacier, the lookout is a popular tourist destination and is staffed by volunteers.

evidence.supports: Standard L-4 plan, dimensions, roof, windows
evidence.quote: Built to standard U.S. Forest Service plans, the one-story ground-level lookout measures fourteen by fourteen feet. The frame structure is capped by a pyramidal roof, and features large windows on all four sides with pivoting shutters that act as sunshades.

evidence.supports: Built 1932 or 1933, one of two intact lookouts, WWII use
evidence.quote: The Suntop lookout was built in either 1932 or 1933 to standard plans for an "L-4 Lookout House." It is one of two intact lookouts from the period in the former Snoqualmie National Forest. The lookout was used during World War II in the U.S. Army Aircraft Warning System.
The lookout was listed on the National Register of Historic Places on July 14, 1987 [1] and the National Historic Lookout Register on September 15, 1994. [4]

evidence.supports: Built 1934, staffed by Snoqualmie Fire Lookout Association volunteers
evidence.quote: The present L-4 cab, built here in 1934, is on the National Historic Lookout Register. It is staffed with volunteers from the Snoqualmie Fire Lookout Association.

As of 2025, the lookout has been renovated inside to reflect fire equipment from 1960s, including some old USFS artifacts such as a crank phone, old helmet, and wire insulators. Other recent efforts added a trail from the parking area, deck around the lookout and a ramp from the south side that enables lookout to be reached by disabled persons.

evidence.supports: Gate locked unless staffed, COVID closure, staffed sometimes
evidence.quote: Lookout is reached by Forest Road 7315. Road is open until last mile-- gate for last mile is generally locked unless lookout is staffed or other work is going on.

corrections.why: The current record's 1934 build date matches only firelookout.com; NHLR and Wikipedia/NRHP both point earlier, to 1932 or 1933.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Build year differs across sources: NHLR says 1932, Wikipedia/NRHP area says 1932 or 1933 (NRHP record area field says 'Built 1933'), and firelookout.com says 1934. All three years are presented rather than picking one.

notes_for_editor: Build year conflict (1932/1933/1934) across three sources, flagged rather than resolved. Brief's own record used 1934; that matches firelookout.com but not NHLR or Wikipedia/NRHP, worth a corrections note if the editor wants to standardize.
